description: CanFlood is Natural Resources Canada's QGIS toolbox for flood-risk modelling. It combines hazard layers, exposed assets and depth-damage or other vulnerability functions to estimate losses and prepare reports. Inputs are location and asset data with flood-depth or probability information; outputs are asset-level and aggregate risk tables, plots and maps. The repository is developed for Canadian applications, while spatial resolution and time horizon follow the supplied hazard and exposure data. Source is free under MIT terms and the maintainers provide versioned documentation and a QGIS 3.34-compatible release. The README records previous fixes to raster preparation, depth-damage curves and dependency versions, which users should consider when reproducing an older run. CanFlood is a workflow, not a national asset inventory or a guarantee that loss functions fit each local building type. It serves flood hazard exposure, risk and adaptation simulations. The catalogue's model-global-river-flood-risk-framework-winsemius-2013 is a separate large-scale flood-risk approach, useful for comparison, not a dependency. This review did not run QGIS or verify outputs.
